name: Jolt Physics (JoltPhysics.js)
role: Jolt rigid-body and soft-body physics as WASM in Node or the browser, stepped at a fixed timestep
summary: JoltPhysics.js (npm jolt-physics) compiles Jolt's C++ engine to WebAssembly. A JoltInterface steps the world by a fixed dt, so positions are read per frame and cached as a trajectory. Beyond Rapier and Matter.js it documents soft bodies and cloth; the fixture covers only rigid spheres on a floor.
use_when: Rigid-body motion baked to per-frame transforms in Node and replayed in a scene
Soft bodies or cloth beside Three.js, which Rapier does not provide (untested here)
Over matter-js for 3D; over rapier when soft bodies are wanted
avoid_when: A few 2D bodies in the browser: matter-js
3D rigid bodies with snapshots and an upstream determinism guide: rapier
Scripted motion with no collisions: anime-js or theatre-js
notes: 2026-11-27: Bake, do not seek: step every frame from t=0 and cache transforms. The npm WASM build reproduced a byte-identical trajectory across two Node processes on one machine; cross-platform determinism is a Jolt compile-time option and is unverified.

assessment.rationale: npm jolt-physics 1.1.2 published 2026-11-21; MIT for bindings and engine; installs with one pnpm dependency and runs in Node with no browser. Adds soft bodies and cloth to the rigid-body neighbours rapier and matter-js; the soft-body claim is documented, not yet tested.

evidence.result: Three spheres dropped on a floor, 90 steps at 1/30 s in Node 22.19.0; trajectory JSON identical across two processes (SHA-256 20046d1d…b132), all finite, bounced and settled at y 0.50, 0.52, 0.68, min y 0.4346.
evidence.scope: Rigid spheres on a static box, wasm build, one machine (macOS arm64); not soft bodies, cloth, other platforms, seeking, or Three.js playback. Settling is incomplete by frame 89.
